newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus bourse to allow offshore listings.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus bourse to allow offshore listings.

text.p: The Cyprus central bank has given the go-ahead for Cyprus's key offshore sector to list on the island's stock exchange provided firms meet listing requirements, bank and exchange officials said on Wednesday.
The key to offshore listings on the 42-share bourse was a central bank decision in February to lift a requirement of bank references for the transaction of titles in offshores, they said.
"This basically opens the door for the flotation of offshore companies on the exchange," Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) director Nondas Metaxas told Reuters.

Transactions in shares of offshores, which must be public companies and meet CSE listing requirements, will be available to non-residents and transactions will be in foreign currencies, the bourse director said.
"Some companies have been making inquiries and have sent us prospectus" said Metaxas. "There is very strong interest."
The registration of offshores is already provided for in regulations of the CSE, which started operations a year ago. Listing requirements are the same for Cypriot and offshore companies, he said.
Nearly 28,000 companies have registered on an offshore basis in Cyprus over the past 20 years. Roughly half of them are operational and 1,100 maintain a permanent presence on the island.
Cyprus has a thriving offshore sector, which includes shipping companies.
Offshore companies contribute around 4.5 percent to Cyprus's gross national product, according to the central bank.

"The Central Bank has no objections if the offshore companies satisfy the requirements of the stock exchange and if they are in the legal form of a public company," Dr Sophocles Michaelides, head of the offshore department of the central bank told Reuters.
Cyprus offers a series of tax breaks for offshores, one of the most attractive being a flat tax rate of 4.25 percent on net income and exemptions on value added tax.
Local companies pay a 20 percent corporate tax on net income up to 40,000 pounds ($77,500) and 25 percent above that figure. ($=0.516 pounds)
